$comment: A prospect profile. One file per prospect; the seeder builds an entire
agency from it. Nothing here is real: the portfolio, the people and the
money are invented to be plausible at this scale, and the only true things
are the agency's name and the portfolio size they told us.
Every date is expressed as an offset from the run, never a literal, so the
world is current whenever it is seeded. A demo with last March's invoices
on screen is the detail that loses the room.

agency.name: Midnight Masquerade
agency.addressText: 2nd Floor, The Foundry, Prestwich Street, Green Point, Cape Town, 8005
agency.$commentManagementFee: UNCONFIRMED. The client has not given us their management fee; 8% is a placeholder that nevertheless appears on the owner record during the demo. Replace it the moment they say a number, and do not quote it back to them as though it came from them.
agency.$commentVat: Client says they are VAT-registered. No number given yet: enter the real one in Settings > VAT, do not invent one (it prints on tax invoices). Every building below is residential, and residential rent is VAT-exempt (VAT Act s12(c)), so no rent invoice carries VAT unless a building is let commercially: set "commercial": true on that building.

branding.$comment: Built for the dark deployment (DEPLOYMENT_THEME=dark): the brand has to read on a near-black ground, so it is a luminous mint rather than a deep green. The same agency on a light deployment would need a darker value — which brand colour reads depends on the surface, and that is config, not a bug.

subscription.$comment: 500 units is past GROWTH_MAX_UNITS (499), so this is a Custom-tier conversation by the platform's own maths — not a sales posture. unitRateCents is read from CUSTOM_UNIT_RATE when left null.

portfolio.$comment: 500 units across a believable Cape Town spread: a few large blocks carry the bulk, a long tail of small buildings and houses makes up the rest. The seeder generates units to hit `units` exactly.

people.$comment: Staff and the two app logins. Every address in this world is on `agency.emailDomain` — Mailpit intercepts by SMTP host, not by domain, so it catches them all, and one domain means nothing on screen says Locare during a white-label demo. The ones marked `watch` are the mailboxes opened on screen.
people.$commentOwners: Invented, like everyone here. Between them and the demo landlord every building has an owner — without that there is no owner statement for most of the book. None of these has a login; only the demo landlord does.

story.$comment: The handful of records that get opened on screen. Everything else is generated filler that only has to survive a scroll; these have to survive a click.

$comment: How much past to generate. Twelve months gives the reports something to draw and makes the account look lived-in rather than created this morning.

arrearsRate is the share of leases OUTSIDE the story that carry an unpaid month (a quarter of those are two months behind). It exists because a book in which every invoice is paid is the tell that the data was generated. Set it to whatever arrears picture the room should see; 0.05 is a plausible figure for a managed book, not a measured one.
